newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium fixes terms for minor bank privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Belgium fixes terms for minor bank privatisation.

text.p: The Belgian government set in motion on Friday the privatisation of minor publicly-owned bank Beroepskrediet/Credit Professionel, fixing the criteria a potential buyer would have to fulfil.

"The sale procedure will begin once the committee for the evaluation of state assets has finished its valuation of (the bank)," the government said in a statement released at the end of its weekly cabinet meeting.

The government said a future "majority shareholder" of the bank must be a private institution, capable of guaranteeing the bank's niche lending to small and medium-sized companies as well as respecting collective labour agreements with its employees.

The bank, formerly called National Kas voor het Beroepskrediet/Caisse Nationale de Credit Professionel, in 1995 ranked 28th among all banks active in Belgium when measured in terms of total assets, according to the country's banking association.
The bank is one of two the government is due to privatise this year as part of plans to raise more than 30 billion Belgian francs in asset sales.

Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Thursday however that the amount expected to be raised from the sale of Credit Professionel was negligible compared with the much larger amount the state expects to garner from the further sale of shares in ASLK-CGER bank and insurance group. -- Nick Antonovics, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6817, Fax +32 2 230 7710
